newsitem.title: USA: Musicland says it met bank covenants.
newsitem.headline: Musicland says it met bank covenants.

text.p: Musicland Stores Corp, which earlier reported a third-quarter loss, said Wednesday it met its bank covenants despite slow sales during the period.

Musicland earlier posted a loss of $16.1 million, or $0.48 per share, for the third quarter. This compared to a loss of $144.6 million or $4.28 a share a year ago, which included a $138 million or $4.09 a share write-down of goodwill.

Revenues rose 2.5 percent to $366.6 million from $357.6 million a year ago. The company said it has closed 79 stores, including 11 Media Play stores, since September 1995. Sales also were hurt by a weaker new release schedule compared to last year, when a Selena album and the video product, "Star Wars Trilogy," were released, Musicland said.

"We are pleased that the company met its bank covenants for the third quarter despite the slow sales growth and without relying on the amendment which was retroactively granted by the bank group on October 18. Our capital management programs reduced short-term borrowing by approximately $30 million compared to the previous year," said Jack W. Eugster, chairman and chief executive officer.
